properties.description: FeNi Oxide Nanotube on Nickel Foam

nodes.name: One-step MOF-74 synthesis
nodes.procedure: Hexagonal nanorods of FeCoNi-MOF-74 supported on nickel foam (denoted as FeCoNi-MOF-74/NF) were synthesized via a one-step synthetic procedure using 2,5-dihydroterephalic acid (DOT; as ligand) and metal node, in which NF acted not only the support but also the source of Ni²⁺ for the formation of trimetallic FeCoNi-MOF-74 (Scheme 1a, Figure S1, and Table S1).
nodes.source_text: MOF-74 with one dimensional channel structure is assembled from 2,5-dihydroterephalic acid (DOT; as ligand) and metal node... FeCoNi-MOF-74/NF were synthesized via a one-step synthetic procedure (Scheme 1a, Figure S1, and Table S1)

nodes.name: In situ electrochemical oxidation
nodes.procedure: The FeCoNi-MOF-74 nanorods were treated with an in situ electrochemical oxidation process at a potential window of 1.0–1.6 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in 1 M KOH solution (cf. Scheme 1a and Figure S3, and also experimental details in Supporting Information). The conversion occurs through enhanced Kirkendall effect where ions of Fe, Co, and Ni are released from decomposed FeCoNi-MOF-74 and react with OH⁻ from electrolyte.

unit_operations.name: Electrochemical Oxidation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: treated with an in situ electrochemical oxidation process at a potential window of 1.0–1.6 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in 1 M KOH solution

nodes.source_text: The FeCoNi-MOF-74 nanorods were treated with an in situ electrochemical oxidation process at a potential window of 1.0–1.6 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in 1 M KOH solution

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: LSV that was operated at a scan rate of 2 mV s⁻¹ in a three-electrode electrochemical cell with an aqueous solution of 1 M KOH as electrolyte... overpotential of 216 mV... Tafel slope of 32 mV dec⁻¹... ultra-low overpotential of 257 mV at... 200 mA cm⁻²... chronoamperometric test at a constant overpotential of 216 and 257 mV... current density can be well retained for up to 24 h

nodes.description: Benchmark OER performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: notably superior to the commercially available benchmark OER electrocatalyst of RuO₂ supported on NF (overpotential of 267 mV and Tafel slope of 49 mV dec⁻¹)... RuO₂/NF can only deliver a much higher overpotential of 323 mV at a much lower current density of 100 mA cm⁻²

nodes.source_text: FeCoNiOxHy/NF (Fe0.5Co0.5NiOxHy/NF) shows the lowest Rct1 (0.08 Ω) and Rct2 (3.48 Ω), which thus indicates the superior electrical conductivity and catalytic activity

nodes.description: Double-layer capacitance measurement for ECSA in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: FeCoNiOₓHᵧ/NF shows a Cdl (0.25 μF cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiOxHy nanotubes show rough surfaces, 70-300 nm diameter, 0.3-1.1 μm length.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After electrochemical oxidation, the size of each nanorod does not change notably (70-300 nm in diameter and 0.3-1.1 μm in length; Figure 1e), but its surface becomes rough.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with fibrous or nanowire morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi-MOF-74 shows solid nanorods. FeCoNiOxHy shows tubular nanostructures of ultra-thin nanosheets ca. 1.5 nm thick with poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image, EDX element maps and line scans reveal that the solid nanorod of FeCoNi-MOF-74 are converted into tubular nanostructures (nanotubes) consisted of ultra-thin nanosheets.

TEM image with two annotated regions
bright field TEM image showing elongated nanostructures
dark field TEM image showing bright Co nanoparticles

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, Ni in both FeCoNi-MOF-74 and FeCoNiOxHy nanotubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDX) area maps indicate the homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, and Ni in FeCoNi-MOF-74 ... and Fe, Co, and Ni still distribute homogeneously in each nanotube.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi-MOF-74 has Fe:Co:Ni = 0.59:0.63:1. FeCoNiOxHy has Fe:Co:Ni = 0.30:0.48:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe:Co:Ni atomic ratio is quantified to be 0.59:0.63:1 by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES; Table S2) ... The Fe:Co:Ni atomic ratio in nanotubes is determined to be 0.30:0.48:1 by ICP-AES.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi-MOF-74 PXRD matches simulated MOF-74. FeCoNiOxHy shows poor crystallinity with hardly any characteristic diffraction peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of trimetallic FeCoNi-MOF-74 is further confirmed by its power X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern, which agrees well with the simulated one ... The poor crystallinity nature of our product is further confirmed by its PXRD pattern, which hardly show any characteristic diffraction peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiOxHy nanosheets show ultrasmall crystalline grains 2-6 nm with lattice spacings 0.215 nm (103) and 0.231 nm (200) of hydrated nickel hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images of the ultra-thin nanosheets in a nanotube show that the nanosheets are ca. 1.5 nm in thickness and feature a poor crystallinity nature ... ultrasmall crystalline grains (2-6 nm). The ultrasmall crystalline grains ... shows two set of plane spacing of 0.215 and 0.231 nm corresponding to the (103) and (200) plane of hydrated nickel hydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiOxHy has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 111 m²/g and hierarchical pores 1.2-9.0 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N2-sorption measurements imply that FeCoNiOxHy have a large Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 111 m² g⁻¹ and hierarchical pores with size ranging from 1.2 to 9.0 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiOxHy shows Fe³⁺ (Fe 2p3/2 711.76 eV, 2p1/2 725.26 eV), Ni²⁺ (Ni 2p3/2 856.33 eV, 2p1/2 874.03 eV), mixed Co³⁺/Co²⁺ with Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio 1.2, and M-OH at 531.42-532.59 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution XPS spectra of Fe, Co, and Ni reveal that these three elements exist in different valence states in FeCoNiOxHy ... Fe exists exclusively in the form of Fe³⁺ ... Ni also exists in only one valence state of Ni²⁺ ... Co exists in two valence states ... Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio to 1.2 for FeCoNiOxHy.
